insight.title: Why the Slinky Was Invented
insight.subtitle: How a failed World War II naval experiment created an iconic toy that still fills playrooms today.
insight.notificationHook: The Slinky was a WWII military accident

sections.text: The walking, coiled Slinky in your toy box wasn't designed for kids. It was originally engineered as a high-tech military device to keep battleships from losing their navigation instruments in heavy seas.

In 1943, mechanical engineer Richard James was designing sensitive tension springs for the Navy. When he accidentally knocked a prototype off a shelf, it didn't crash—it gracefully stepped down to the floor.
James realized the mesmerizing "walking" motion was pure entertainment. Millions of sales later, the exact same steel formulation and coil tension rules still govern every Slinky produced today.
A military failure that walked straight into history.
